top_story.headline: Navy awards Raytheon $6.1 billion in missile deals without competition, citing the public interest
top_story.dek: Three Standard Missile awards invoke a rarely used exception that requires the agency head's own determination and written notice to Congress.
paragraphs: The Naval Sea Systems Command awarded Raytheon Company a $5,905,358,647 multiyear contract on September 30 for fiscal 2026 production of the Standard Missile 6, without competition. The award notice, posted October 6, cites 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(7). That is the public-interest exception, which lets an agency skip competition only on the agency head's own determination and with written notice to Congress.

Two more Raytheon awards in the same window cite the same exception. One is a $160,892,270 undefinitized contract action on September 24 to move the Standard Missile 6 Block IAU, which the notice calls "a critical obsolescence upgrade," toward full-rate production. The other is $69,051,583 on September 29 for Standard Missile 2 test equipment and Standard Missile 6 spares. Together the three total $6,135,302,500. None of the three notices has a justification document or the public-interest determination attached.

These are the largest of several no-bid missile awards in this edition. Strategic Systems Programs, the Navy office behind the Trident II D5 missile, added $194.1 million in sole-source fire-control work on the Nuclear-Armed, Sea-Launched Cruise Missile for General Dynamics Mission Systems. Separately, the Defense Logistics Agency plans to sole-source depot test equipment for Ukraine's PATRIOT air-defense system to Raytheon.

sections.headline: Federal Highway Administration plans a $9.8 million no-bid deal with a mobility-data nonprofit that has no federal contract on record
paragraphs: 125 new sole-source and limited-source justifications this edition. 101 of them were posted under other notice types (50 as Special Notices, 44 as Award Notices, 7 as Sources Sought), and no repeats from earlier editions were left out. The biggest by value is a $297.7 million extension of the health department's Ebola-drug contract with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

blocks.title: Highway agency picks a mobility-data nonprofit with no federal contract on record for a $9.8 million no-bid standards deal
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Federal Highway Administration plans a five-year contract with a $9,800,000 ceiling and a $25,000 minimum for the Open Mobility Foundation, a Massachusetts nonprofit, to develop and maintain transportation data standards for the Department of Transportation's Intelligent Transportation Systems Joint Program Office. The agency calls the foundation "uniquely qualified" because it governs the Mobility Data Specification and Curb Data Specification, which the notice says are used in more than 1,200 cities. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this name. The agency posted the notice as a Special Notice, not as a Justification.

blocks.title: Air Force skips competition to hire one named airshow boss for Dover's 2027 open house
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Department of the Air Force intends to give Wm. David Schultz a no-bid contract to run flight operations, narration, sound and ground support at the Dover Air Force Base, Delaware, open house on June 5-6, 2027, according to the draft work statement. That statement requires 200 hours of airshow work with warbirds, experience with crowds of more than 100,000 and past work with the Thunderbirds, Blue Angels or Snowbirds. The contractor is paid 100% of the fee if on site but unable to perform for reasons outside their control. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this name. The notice was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: Marine Corps gives L3Harris a $96.9 million no-bid follow-on for satellite terminals, citing its control of the technical data
meta: Only one company can do it
U.S. Marine Corps, Department of the Navy
blocks.text: The U.S. Marine Corps awarded L3Harris Technologies a sole-source follow-on contract on September 28 worth up to $96,905,058 for more Marine Corps Wideband Satellite–Expeditionary terminals (the Panther II), plus spares, upgrades and training. The justification cites a March 2025 decision to add 313 terminals and says "L3Harris alone holds the Technical Data Package" and controls the firmware and software licenses needed to keep the terminal running. It also notes that the current contract was awarded in 2020 through full and open competition. The agency posted it as an Award Notice.

blocks.title: Health department adds $297.7 million to Regeneron's no-bid Ebola-drug contract, pushing it to nearly $1 billion
meta: Only one company can do it
Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, Department of Health and Human Services
blocks.text: The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority at the Department of Health and Human Services justified a $297,715,850.15 modification to its contract with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals for Inmazeb, Regeneron's Ebola treatment. The change raises the contract from $693,056,926.67 to $990,772,776.82 and covers up to 26,500 doses for the Strategic National Stockpile or vendor-managed inventory through 2031. The justification says Inmazeb and/or Ebanga, another Ebola therapeutic, were used in each of six Ebola outbreaks between January 2021 and January 2025.

sections.headline: Navy gives Raytheon $5.9 billion for Standard Missile 6 production under the public-interest exception
paragraphs: 1,629 new award notices this edition; one whose solicitation was listed in an earlier edition (a 2024 award) is left out. Beyond the Raytheon missile awards, the Navy's nuclear-missile office made several large no-bid awards, and one award notice lists a $1.5 billion value where its own text says $15.1 million.

blocks.title: Navy awards Raytheon $6.1 billion in three Standard Missile deals without competition, citing the public interest
meta: Naval Sea Systems Command, Department of the Navy
blocks.text: The Naval Sea Systems Command awarded Raytheon Company a $5,905,358,647 multiyear contract on September 30 for fiscal 2026 Standard Missile 6 production. The award was sole-source under 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(7), the public-interest exception, which requires the agency head's own determination and written notice to Congress. Two related awards cite the same exception: $160,892,270 on September 24 to move the upgraded Standard Missile 6 Block IAU into production, and $69,051,583 on September 29 for Standard Missile 2 test equipment and Standard Missile 6 spares. None of the three notices has a justification document attached.

blocks.title: Navy's nuclear-missile office adds $194 million in no-bid fire-control work for the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile
meta: Strategic Systems Programs, Department of the Navy
blocks.text: Strategic Systems Programs gave General Dynamics Mission Systems of Pittsfield, Massachusetts, a sole-source contract modification on September 3 for technical and engineering support to the fire-control work on the Nuclear-Armed, Sea-Launched Cruise Missile program. The modification covers fiscal 2026 through 2028 on a cost-plus-fixed-fee basis and includes options to raise the level of effort by up to 30%. The notice lists $194,139,485 and was posted October 8, five weeks after the award.

blocks.title: Navy pays an Arizona state agency $8.5 million to store Trident missile rocket motors
meta: Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs
Strategic Systems Programs, Department of the Navy
blocks.text: Strategic Systems Programs gave a sole-source contract to the Arizona Department of Emergency and Military Affairs, a state agency rather than a company. The work is receiving, handling and storing large rocket motors for the Trident II D5 submarine-launched ballistic missile at Camp Navajo in Bellemont, Arizona, and the $8,473,053 award is dated October 1.

sections.headline: Army raises Striveworks software contract ceiling tenfold, to $700 million
paragraphs: 206 new special notices this edition, with no repeats from earlier editions left out. The space agency also asked states to pitch sites for a new U.S. Space Academy created by executive order.

blocks.title: Army raises Striveworks' single-award software contract ceiling tenfold, to $700.1 million
meta: Army Contracting Command–Aberdeen Proving Ground, Department of the Army
blocks.text: Army Contracting Command–Aberdeen Proving Ground modified its single-award contract with Striveworks Inc. of Austin, Texas, adding $630,140,000 to the ceiling, which takes it from $70,000,000 to $700,140,000. The five-year ordering period began January 15, 2026, and did not change, so the increase came less than nine months into the contract. The notice describes the work only by its industry code, custom computer programming.

blocks.title: Space agency asks states to bid to host a new U.S. Space Academy created by executive order
blocks.text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration invited each state to submit one official proposal to host the United States Space Academy. The academy is a new civilian federal institution, led by the space agency, that President Donald J. Trump established in Executive Order 14423 on August 28, 2026. The request asks for a rough estimate of the cost to set up the academy at each proposed site and the resources that state and local governments and partners would contribute. The agency's question-and-answer file says the order requires a commission to send the President recommendations, including a process for choosing a permanent location, by December 26, 2026.

sections.headline: Immigration agency seeks an 'SI-powered' system to monitor detainee calls and video and build voice profiles
paragraphs: 384 new sources-sought notices this edition, with no repeats from earlier editions left out. Also notable: the Secret Service is looking for vehicle-armor designers, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation wants franchise restaurants in its Washington headquarters.

blocks.title: Immigration agency seeks an 'SI-powered' system to mine detainee calls, messages and video, and to build voice profiles
meta: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Department of Homeland Security
blocks.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement wants information on an "Integrated SI-Powered Detention Communications and Video Intelligence Suite" for its detention facilities. According to the attached requirements, the system would correlate detainees' phone, messaging, tablet, video-visitation and camera data and would "create and improve voice profiles from authorized existing recordings without requiring a separate enrollment session, subject cooperation, or new recording hardware." It would also flag fights, crowd formation and person-down events and run automated headcounts against the roster. In a separate notice the same day, the agency's technology office defined SI as "Super Intelligence."

blocks.title: Secret Service looks for companies to design and fit new armor for its vehicles
meta: U.S. Secret Service, Department of Homeland Security
blocks.text: The U.S. Secret Service is asking companies about designing new armor systems, modifying existing armor designs with preselected materials, and fitting approved armor into cars and non-military specialty vehicles. The request document says contractor staff who need classified access must hold Secret clearances. No value or vehicle count is given.

blocks.title: Federal Bureau of Investigation wants franchise restaurant brands inside its Washington headquarters
meta: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is asking whether it could deal directly with individual food franchise brands, rather than one master food-service contractor, to run food service in the J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. It asks about franchise terms, royalties, buildout costs and any precedent for franchises inside federal buildings or military bases. The notice was posted October 8 but lists a response deadline of September 21, 2026.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files were approved October 5 to 10
paragraphs: Neither openomb.org nor a direct scan of apportionment-public.max.gov turned up a new Office of Management and Budget apportionment file between October 5 and October 10, so nothing was flagged. Of 145 spend plans checked, none was new or changed.

So the apportionments section was written directly from the apportionment data, and the ethics section was left out. Of those, 998 large files are queued and will be read over the next editions, 90 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 2 have no extractable text (video, CAD and similar). 1,920 links to outside portals (mostly DIBBS) were not followed.
